entities.name: GlmU bifunctional enzyme
observations: 458 aa basic bacterial protein; predicted molecular mass 50.55 kDa and pI 9.87.
High-coverage homology supports bifunctional GlmU assignment: 40.2–44.7% identity over 97.6–98.9% sequence coverage to reviewed references Q0I1G0, B0UW09, and B3H116.
N-terminal region is consistent with nucleotide-sugar pyrophosphorylase activity; C-terminal region is consistent with glucosamine-1-phosphate N-acetyltransferase activity.
Reference GlmU proteins are cytoplasmic homotrimers and bind one Mg2+ per subunit; these properties are homology-supported, not directly experimentally established for this query sequence.
Pfam matches include NTP-transferase-family domains near residues 5–210 and GMPPB_C/Hexapep-family signatures in the C-terminal half.

source_tools.relevance: Sequence properties, Pfam matches, and homology/function evidence

entities.name: GlcN-1-P acetylation
observations: Glucosamine-1-phosphate + acetyl-CoA → N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + CoA + H+; EC 2.3.1.157; Rhea RHEA:13725.
This is the acetyltransferase reaction assigned to the C-terminal GlmU domain.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc formation
observations: N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate + UTP + H+ → UDP-N-acetylglucosamine + diphosphate; EC 2.7.7.23; Rhea RHEA:13509.
This is the UDP-N-acetylglucosamine diphosphorylase reaction assigned to the N-terminal GlmU domain and requires Mg2+ in reference proteins.

entities.name: UDP-GlcNAc biosynthesis
observations: GlmU catalyzes the final two sequential steps of bacterial de novo UDP-N-acetylglucosamine biosynthesis, supplying precursor for peptidoglycan and, in some bacteria, lipid A biosynthesis.

source_tools.relevance: Curated pathway annotation from reviewed GlmU homologs
